children: Shares extend their recovery as analysts argue SpaceX’s growth can justify its valuation. Launch milestones and the next earnings report will test that optimism.
Morgan Stanley gives the rally fresh support
SpaceX
climbed 7.6% to $171.09 Monday, following Friday’s 7.35% advance. Together, those sessions produced a roughly 15.5% gain, calculated from closing prices.
Shares now stand about 27% above June’s $135 IPO price, extending their recovery after a volatile opening few months.
Morgan Stanley maintained its Overweight rating and $300 price target, describing the stock as “cheap and getting cheaper” relative to growth prospects.
That target implies roughly 75% upside from Monday’s close, but represents the bank’s assessment of potential value rather than a certain destination.
The valuation argument needs context. At Friday’s price, SpaceX traded around 30 times expected 2028 operating profit, versus 16 times for Big Tech peers.
Morgan Stanley’s growth-adjusted comparison looks more favorable. The implication: investors are paying a premium today because they expect profits to expand faster.
SpaceXSI is the new SpaceXAI?
Elon Musk said on X he plans to rename SpaceXAI, the AI unit of the company, as SpaceXSI, adopting “super intelligence” after President Donald Trump pushed the terminology.

The announcement reinforces Musk’s positioning of SpaceX as an AI business alongside its space operations, although a new name alone provides no evidence of improved technology or financial performance.
The financial commitment is more tangible. Second-quarter revenue
, up from $4.1 billion a year earlier, while capital expenditure exceeded $18 billion.
AI accounted for $15.8 billion of that spending. Management said similarly heavy investment would continue over the following quarters.

Starlink ended June with 12 million subscribers, twice the year-earlier total, but monthly revenue per subscriber fell to $66 from $85. International expansion and cheaper plans contributed to the decline.
Launches and earnings provide the next tests

SpaceX plans to reattempt its postponed Space Development Agency mission Tuesday, continuing a busy launch schedule. The Falcon 9 mission carries satellites for a defense communications constellation, highlighting the government business that sits alongside Starlink subscriptions.
Starship Flight 15 is expected later this month, with Morgan Stanley identifying it as another catalyst. Progress toward reusability could improve launch economics and support satellite deployment.

The next quarterly report will bring those expectations back to revenue and costs. A full quarter of Anthropic’s computing contract should offer clearer evidence of AI monetization, while Starlink’s figures will show how subscriber growth and pricing interact.

title: SPCX: SpaceX Jumps 7.6% as Morgan Stanley Backs Growth Outlook. Also, a New Name?
